title: Daniel Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Daniel chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Daniel Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Daniel Chapter 6.

questions.question: In Daniel 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Darius setting over the kingdom an hundred and twenty princes
Daniel praying three times a day
The decree to not ask any God or man
Daniel being preferred above the presidents
questions.correctAnswer: Darius setting over the kingdom an hundred and twenty princes
questions.explanation: This event is mentioned first in the chapter, in Daniel 6:1 where Darius sets over the kingdom an hundred and twenty princes.

questions.question: Who was preferred above the presidents and princes?
questions.correctAnswer: Daniel
questions.explanation: Daniel was preferred because an excellent spirit was in him, as stated in Daniel 6:3.

questions.question: What did the presidents and princes seek to find against Daniel?
options: Occasion against him concerning the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: Occasion against him concerning the kingdom
questions.explanation: The presidents and princes sought to find occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom, as stated in Daniel 6:4.

questions.question: According to the text, what was found in Daniel?
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: The text states that Daniel was faithful, and no error or fault was found in him, as stated in Daniel 6:4.

questions.question: What did the men decide regarding finding occasion against Daniel?
options: To find it concerning the law of his God
questions.correctAnswer: To find it concerning the law of his God
questions.explanation: The men concluded that they would not find any occasion against Daniel except concerning the law of his God, as stated in Daniel 6:5.

questions.question: How many presidents assembled together to the king?
questions.correctAnswer: All of them
questions.explanation: All the presidents of the kingdom assembled together to the king, as stated in Daniel 6:6.

questions.question: What did the presidents and princes ask King Darius to establish?
questions.correctAnswer: A royal statute
questions.explanation: They consulted together to establish a royal statute, as stated in Daniel 6:7.

questions.question: What was the punishment for asking a petition of any God or man besides King Darius?
options: To be cast into the den of lions
questions.correctAnswer: To be cast into the den of lions
questions.explanation: The decree stated that whoever shall ask a petition of any God or man for thirty days, except of the king, would be cast into the den of lions, as mentioned in Daniel 6:7.

questions.question: What did King Darius do with the writing and the decree?
questions.correctAnswer: He signed it
questions.explanation: King Darius signed the writing and the decree, as stated in Daniel 6:9.

questions.question: How many times a day did Daniel pray?
questions.correctAnswer: Three times
questions.explanation: Daniel kneeled upon his knees three times a day and prayed, as stated in Daniel 6:10.

questions.question: Toward which city did Daniel open his windows when he prayed?
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Daniel's windows were open toward Jerusalem when he prayed, as stated in Daniel 6:10.

questions.question: True or False: Daniel had an excellent spirit in him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The text states that Daniel had an excellent spirit in him, as stated in Daniel 6:3.

questions.question: True or False: The presidents and princes were loyal to Daniel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The text indicates that the presidents and princes sought to find occasion against Daniel, showing their lack of loyalty, as stated in Daniel 6:4.

questions.question: True or False: Daniel prayed only once a day.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text states that Daniel prayed three times a day, as stated in Daniel 6:10.

questions.question: True or False: King Darius established a law that allowed prayer to other gods.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The law established by King Darius prohibited asking a petition of any God or man except for him, as stated in Daniel 6:7.

medium.title: Daniel Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Daniel Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What were Daniel's actions that led to the men assembling and finding him in prayer?
options: Daniel was praying and making supplication before his God
Daniel was gathering with other officials in the king's palace
Daniel was hiding and refusing to come out
Daniel was writing a letter to the king
questions.correctAnswer: Daniel was praying and making supplication before his God
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:11 states that the men found Daniel praying and making supplication before his God.

questions.question: What does Daniel 6:16 promise will happen if someone is cast into the den of lions according to Daniel 6:15?
options: The king believes Daniel's God will deliver him
The person will be eaten by the lions
The king will forget about the person
questions.correctAnswer: The king believes Daniel's God will deliver him
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:16 shows the king saying to Daniel that his God whom he serves will deliver him, connecting to the unchangeable law mentioned in 6:15.

questions.question: How did King Darius react upon hearing that Daniel was disobeying the decree?
options: He was sore displeased with himself and tried to save Daniel
He praised the men for their vigilance
questions.correctAnswer: He was sore displeased with himself and tried to save Daniel
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:14 says the king was sore displeased with himself and set his heart on delivering Daniel.

questions.question: What reason did the men give the king to insist that Daniel must be punished despite the king's wish to save him?
options: No decree or statute established by the king can be changed
The king had no authority to pardon anyone
questions.correctAnswer: No decree or statute established by the king can be changed
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:15 explains that the law of the Medes and Persians is that no decree or statute which the king establishes can be changed.

questions.question: What does Daniel’s consistent prayer life, even under threat of death, teach about faithfulness in trials?
options: Faithfulness requires obedience to God even at great personal risk
Prayer is only necessary when one is safe
Avoiding danger is more important than prayer
One should pray only when commanded by authorities
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness requires obedience to God even at great personal risk
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:10 and 6:11 show Daniel praying openly despite the decree, demonstrating faithfulness under threat.

questions.question: How does the king's action of sealing the den with his own signet illustrate the seriousness of the decree?
options: It ensured that the decree concerning Daniel could not be altered
It was a symbolic gesture with no real effect
It allowed the king to change his mind later
It was meant to protect Daniel from harm
questions.correctAnswer: It ensured that the decree concerning Daniel could not be altered
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:17 states the king sealed the den so the purpose concerning Daniel might not be changed.

questions.question: What practical lesson can be learned from King Darius fasting and losing sleep after casting Daniel into the lions' den?
options: True leaders feel the weight of their decisions and seek God in distress
Leaders should always avoid difficult decisions
Fasting is not related to concern for others
A king’s sleep is not affected by his actions
questions.correctAnswer: True leaders feel the weight of their decisions and seek God in distress
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:18 shows the king fasting and losing sleep, indicating his deep concern and reliance on God.

questions.question: Why did Daniel continue to pray facing Jerusalem despite the new law forbidding prayer to anyone but the king?
options: Because he was faithful and obedient to God rather than man
Because he did not know about the law
Because he was trying to disobey the king
Because he wanted to avoid the lions’ den
questions.correctAnswer: Because he was faithful and obedient to God rather than man
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:10 and 6:13 show Daniel's consistent prayer life despite the decree, highlighting his faithfulness to God.

questions.question: How do the accusations against Daniel reveal the nature of integrity in a hostile environment?
options: Integrity may provoke opposition when standing firm in faith
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity may provoke opposition when standing firm in faith
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:4-5 describe how Daniel’s faultless conduct led to accusations based on his faithfulness to God.

questions.question: What does the king’s lamentable voice when calling Daniel from the lions’ den suggest about prayer and hope in crisis?
options: It shows dependence on God’s power to save in desperate times
It indicates doubt in God’s ability
It shows he expected Daniel’s death
It implies the king wanted to punish Daniel
questions.correctAnswer: It shows dependence on God’s power to save in desperate times
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:20 records the king’s lamentable voice and his question about God’s ability to save Daniel.

questions.question: What does the king’s effort to deliver Daniel until sunset reveal about leadership and compassion?
options: Leaders should work persistently to protect the innocent
Leaders must always obey advisors without question
Leaders have no responsibility for their subjects
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders should work persistently to protect the innocent
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:14 describes the king laboring till sunset to save Daniel, showing compassion and leadership responsibility.

questions.question: How does the unchangeable nature of the law of the Medes and Persians (Daniel 6:15) affect the king’s ability to intervene for Daniel?
options: It prevents the king from rescinding the decree
It allows the king to pardon Daniel anytime
It means the law can be altered by the king
It does not affect the king’s decision
questions.correctAnswer: It prevents the king from rescinding the decree
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:15 states that no decree established by the king can be changed, limiting his intervention.

questions.question: What spiritual principle can believers learn from Daniel’s example of praying three times a day despite opposition?
options: Consistent prayer is vital for faithfulness regardless of circumstances
Prayer should be avoided when threatened
One should pray only in secret
questions.correctAnswer: Consistent prayer is vital for faithfulness regardless of circumstances
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:10-11 shows Daniel’s consistent prayer life even under threat, teaching persistence in prayer.

questions.question: True or False: The king felt no remorse or concern after ordering Daniel to be cast into the lions’ den.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:14 and 6:18 describe the king’s displeasure and fasting, showing his deep concern.

questions.question: True or False: The law of the Medes and Persians could be changed by the king if he desired.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:15 clearly states that the law of the Medes and Persians does not permit any decree or statute to be changed.

hard.title: Daniel Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Daniel Chapter 6.

questions.question: What did Daniel say to the king after being rescued from the lions' den?
questions.correctAnswer: O king, live for ever.
questions.explanation: Daniel said this in Daniel 6:21, expressing respect for the king.

questions.question: Why was Daniel not hurt by the lions?
questions.correctAnswer: He believed in his God.
questions.explanation: This is stated in Daniel 6:23, highlighting Daniel's faith as the reason for his deliverance.

questions.question: What decree did King Darius make after Daniel's deliverance?
options: No one shall pray for thirty days.
All should fear the God of Daniel.
questions.correctAnswer: All should fear the God of Daniel.
questions.explanation: In Daniel 6:26, Darius decreed that everyone should tremble before Daniel's God.

questions.question: What happened to those who accused Daniel?
options: They were cast into the lions' den.
questions.correctAnswer: They were cast into the lions' den.
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:24 records that the king commanded their punishment for falsely accusing Daniel.

questions.question: What did Daniel's God do to the lions?
questions.correctAnswer: Shut their mouths.
questions.explanation: Daniel states in Daniel 6:22 that God sent an angel to shut the lions' mouths.

questions.question: How did King Darius feel after Daniel was found unharmed?
questions.correctAnswer: Exceedingly glad
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:23 indicates that the king was exceedingly glad when he learned Daniel was unharmed.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'מָלָךְ' (malakh) in Daniel 6:22 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Angel
questions.explanation: 'מָלָךְ' (malakh) is often translated as 'angel' and refers to a divine messenger, as seen in Daniel 6:22.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Daniel's declaration of innocence in Daniel 6:22?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: The structure of the statements regarding Daniel's innocence reflects a parallelism in his claims before God and the king.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of God's deliverance as seen in Daniel 6:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 34:7
questions.explanation: Psalm 34:7 echoes God's deliverance theme, stating that the angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear Him.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of faith under persecution as seen in Daniel 6:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 11:6
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:6 highlights the importance of faith in God, connecting to Daniel's resolve to pray despite the decree.

questions.question: What comes before Daniel 6:15?
options: Daniel is thrown into the den.
questions.correctAnswer: The king is displeased.
questions.explanation: Before Daniel 6:15, the king expresses his displeasure and concern for Daniel in verse 14.

questions.question: What does Daniel 6:28 indicate about Daniel's future?
questions.correctAnswer: He will prosper.
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:28 states that Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and Cyrus, indicating his continued favor.

questions.question: Daniel was known for having an excellent spirit. What does this imply about his character?
questions.correctAnswer: He was trustworthy and competent.
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:3 indicates that his excellent spirit was recognized by the king, suggesting his integrity and skill.

questions.question: Is it true that King Darius fasted the night Daniel was in the lions' den?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:18 states that King Darius fasted the night while Daniel was in the den, showing his concern.

questions.question: Is it false that Daniel was thrown into the lions' den for committing a crime?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Daniel was not guilty of any crime; he was cast into the den due to his faithfulness to God, as noted in Daniel 6:4.

theological.title: Daniel Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Daniel Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Daniel 6:3 teach about God's nature as it relates to human excellence and divine favor?
options: God bestows an excellent spirit on His servants, marking them for favor and leadership
Human wisdom and strength are the sole basis for promotion in God's kingdom
God’s favor is unrelated to a person’s spiritual character
Divine favor is only given after miraculous signs
questions.correctAnswer: God bestows an excellent spirit on His servants, marking them for favor and leadership
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:3 states that Daniel was preferred above others because an excellent spirit was in him, indicating that God’s favor is connected to the impartation of an excellent spirit.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin is illustrated by the actions of the presidents and princes in Daniel 6:4?
options: Sinful human nature leads to envy and attempts to undermine the faithful
Human nature is inherently cooperative and just
Sin does not affect political leadership
God’s providence prevents all human scheming
questions.correctAnswer: Sinful human nature leads to envy and attempts to undermine the faithful
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:4 reveals that the presidents and princes sought to find fault with Daniel but could not, showing sinful envy and opposition toward the godly.

questions.question: What doctrine about salvation and divine protection does Daniel 6:22 teach?
options: God sends His angel to protect the innocent from harm
Salvation is only through human effort and political influence
God’s protection is arbitrary and unpredictable
Divine intervention is a myth in the face of physical danger
questions.correctAnswer: God sends His angel to protect the innocent from harm
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:22 explicitly states that God sent His angel to shut the lions’ mouths, protecting Daniel because innocence was found in him before God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Daniel 6:26 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:26 declares God as the living God whose kingdom shall not be destroyed and whose dominion is everlasting, highlighting His sovereignty over all.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly exemplified in Daniel 6:9 when the king signs the irrevocable decree?
questions.correctAnswer: Immutability
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:9 shows the decree’s unchangeable nature according to the law of the Medes and Persians, reflecting the attribute of immutability or unchanging nature of divine and royal laws.

questions.question: How does Daniel 6:10 prepare for the New Testament theme of faithful prayer under persecution?
options: It models steadfast prayer despite hostile decrees, anticipating Christ's teaching on persistent prayer
It discourages prayer when laws forbid it
It shows that public prayer is always politically safe
It suggests prayer is optional under threat
questions.correctAnswer: It models steadfast prayer despite hostile decrees, anticipating Christ's teaching on persistent prayer
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:10 shows Daniel continuing his regular prayers despite the new law, prefiguring the New Testament emphasis on faithful prayer amid opposition (cf. Luke 18:1).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Daniel 6:16–17 have to the motif of intercession and divine deliverance in Scripture?
options: The king’s hope in Daniel’s God resembles intercessory hope found in the Psalms and prophetic deliverance narratives
It denies the possibility of divine rescue
It portrays the king as a divine savior figure
It emphasizes human power over God
questions.correctAnswer: The king’s hope in Daniel’s God resembles intercessory hope found in the Psalms and prophetic deliverance narratives
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:16–17 shows the king expressing confidence in God’s deliverance, paralleling biblical themes of trusting God’s rescue found in Psalms and prophetic contexts.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Daniel 6:4 and 6:22 teach about the relationship between human innocence and divine protection?
options: God’s protection is granted because of human innocence and faithfulness
Divine protection is unrelated to human conduct
God protects all equally regardless of innocence
questions.correctAnswer: God’s protection is granted because of human innocence and faithfulness
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:4 notes Daniel’s innocence and faithfulness, and 6:22 shows God’s angel protecting him, linking innocence to divine protection.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice and human law does Daniel 6:15 and 6:24 jointly illustrate?
options: Human laws have binding power but divine justice ultimately avenges the righteous
Divine justice is limited by human law
Human laws always align perfectly with God’s justice
Divine justice ignores human legal systems
questions.correctAnswer: Human laws have binding power but divine justice ultimately avenges the righteous
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:15 affirms the unchangeable human law, while 6:24 shows divine justice in punishing the accusers, illustrating God's ultimate justice working through human systems.

questions.question: What theological synthesis emerges from Daniel 6:25 and 6:27 regarding the universal reign of God?
options: God’s kingdom is universal, eternal, and demonstrated through signs and wonders
God’s reign is limited to Israel only
God’s kingdom is symbolic and not actual
God’s power is ineffective in the world
questions.correctAnswer: God’s kingdom is universal, eternal, and demonstrated through signs and wonders
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:25 and 6:27 proclaim God’s universal kingdom, eternal dominion, and power evidenced by miracles, emphasizing His sovereign reign over all nations.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Daniel 6:10-23 teaches that God arbitrarily intervenes in human affairs to reward the pious. What does these verses actually teach?
options: God’s intervention is based on innocence and faithfulness, not arbitrary favoritism
God intervenes randomly without regard to human conduct
Intervention depends on political connections rather than faith
Divine rescue is a myth and did not actually occur
questions.correctAnswer: God’s intervention is based on innocence and faithfulness, not arbitrary favoritism
questions.explanation: Verses 10-23 show Daniel’s consistent faith and innocence before God, who sends His angel to protect him, indicating God’s intervention is just and purposeful.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification is evident in Daniel 6:10 concerning Daniel’s prayer practice under persecution?
options: Sanctification involves steadfast devotion to God’s ordinances despite external threats
Sanctification is irrelevant under political pressure
Prayer is only necessary when safe
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves steadfast devotion to God’s ordinances despite external threats
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:10 shows Daniel continuing his regular prayer practice despite the king’s decree, modeling perseverance in holiness amid trial.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exhibited in Daniel 6:22 in the context of God sending His angel to shut the lions' mouths?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:22 demonstrates God’s omnipotence as He exercises sovereign power to control the lions and preserve Daniel.

questions.question: How does Daniel 6:28 fit into the larger biblical narrative of God’s providence over His faithful servants across empires?
options: It affirms God’s providential blessing and success upon His servants despite changing political regimes
It denies God’s involvement in human affairs
It implies success is merely political and unrelated to faith
It contradicts earlier promises of divine protection
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms God’s providential blessing and success upon His servants despite changing political regimes
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:28 shows Daniel prospering under Darius and Cyrus, illustrating God’s providential care across different empires for His faithful ones.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine sovereignty and human authority is taught in Daniel 6:1 and 6:9?
options: God ordains human rulers and their decrees, which are binding until He intervenes
Human rulers act independently of God’s will
Divine sovereignty nullifies all human laws
Human authority is supreme over divine commands
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains human rulers and their decrees, which are binding until He intervenes
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:1 shows Darius’s political structure, and 6:9 shows the binding decree, both demonstrating God’s sovereignty over human authorities and laws.
